passageTranslation:
REGISTRATION — Adult Education Centre North

Surname: Petrova · First name: Elena · Date of birth: 12.03.1995 · Place of birth: Sofia · Nationality: Bulgarian · Address: Hauptstraße 14, 20095 Hamburg · Phone: 0172 55 43 210 · E-mail: e.petrova@mail.de · Mother tongue: Bulgarian · Other languages: English, Russian · Occupation: nurse · Course: German A2, Monday + Wednesday, 6–8 pm · Course start: 7 September · Course fee: 180 euros · Payment: by bank transfer by 1 September · Signature: E. Petrova · Date: 20.08.2026

Note: Please bring your ID and a passport photo on the first day of the course. If you cannot attend the course, please cancel by 31 August. After that, no refund of the course fee is possible. You will receive the course book from the course teacher on the first day.
questions[0].explanation: Geburtsdatum: 12.03.1995 — German dates run day.month.year, so 12.03. is 12 March. 20.08.2026 is the date she signed the form.
questions[1].explanation: Weitere Sprachen: Englisch, Russisch. German is the language she is learning, not one she lists.
questions[1].questionTranslation: Which languages does Elena speak besides Bulgarian?
questions[2].explanation: Zahlung: per Überweisung bis 1. September. bis = by (a deadline).
questions[2].questionTranslation: How must Elena pay the course fee?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[0]: in cash on the first day
questions[3].explanation: Hinweis: Bitte bringen Sie zum ersten Kurstag Ihren Ausweis und ein Passfoto mit. The course book is given to her on that day, not brought.
questions[3].questionTranslation: What must she bring on the first day?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: the course book and a photo
questions[4].explanation: "… melden Sie sich bitte bis zum 31. August ab. Danach ist keine Rückzahlung der Kursgebühr mehr möglich."
questions[4].questionTranslation: By when can Elena cancel the course and get her money back?
questions[4].optionsTranslation[2]: by the first day of the course
help.intro: A registration form, filled in — for a language course, but the fields are the same on every German form you will ever meet: Name / Vorname (surname / first name — in that order!), Geburtsdatum (date of birth, written day.month.year), Geburtsort, Staatsangehörigkeit (nationality — as an adjective: bulgarisch, deutsch), Adresse with the postcode before the town, Muttersprache, Unterschrift (signature), Datum. Sooner or later you fill one in yourself — at the town hall, the doctor's, the gym — and reading one carefully is the first half of that. The traps are conventions rather than words: German dates are 12.03.1995 (12 March), the family name comes first on forms, and Hinweis (note) at the bottom usually carries instructions and deadlines — bis zum 31. August — that become questions. Three dates on the form (birth, signing, course start) and one deadline in the note: read the label before the number.
help.tips[0].title: The standard fields
help.tips[0].text: Name = surname, Vorname = first name. Geburtsdatum (TT.MM.JJJJ), Geburtsort, Staatsangehörigkeit (adjective, lowercase), Adresse (Straße, Hausnummer, PLZ Ort), Telefon, E-Mail, Unterschrift, Datum.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Surname: Petrova · First name: Elena · Nationality: Bulgarian
help.tips[0].trap: 'Name' on a German form means surname. Writing your first name there is the most common form error.
help.tips[0].check.q: Your name is Tom Baker. The form has the fields 'Name:' and 'Vorname:'. What goes after 'Name:'?
help.tips[0].check.why: On a German form, Name means your surname. Tom goes after Vorname.
help.tips[1].title: Dates: day.month.year
help.tips[1].text: 12.03.1995 is the twelfth of March. Written out: am zwölften März. Read the dots as 'day, month, year' and never as the American order.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Date of birth: 12.03.1995 → born on 12 March 1995
help.tips[1].check.q: Geburtsdatum: 05.11.1990 — when was the person born?
help.tips[1].check.why: German dates go day.month.year, so 05.11. is the fifth of November.
help.tips[2].title: Payment and instructions
help.tips[2].text: per Überweisung (by bank transfer), bar (cash), mit Karte; bis 1. September / bis zum 31. August (by …); Bitte bringen Sie … mit (formal imperative + separable mitbringen); sich abmelden (cancel); die Rückzahlung (refund). The Hinweis lines are where the last questions hide.
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Payment: by bank transfer by 1 September.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: If you cannot attend the course, please cancel by 31 August.
help.tips[2].check.q: Hinweis: Bitte bezahlen Sie bis zum 15. Juli. What does „bis zum 15. Juli“ mean?
help.tips[2].check.why: bis (zum) gives a deadline: the payment must arrive on or before that date.
help.remember[0]: Name = surname, Vorname = first name; PLZ before the town; day.month.year.
help.remember[1]: Read the Hinweis: it is an instruction, and instructions become questions.
help.exam: Forms like this appear in the reading and writing of the A2 exam — and at every German town hall, surgery and language school.
help.hook: Fill in any German form without slips: surname first, dates as day.month.year, and the note that hides the deadline.
